column1: A new study conducted for the World Bank by Murdoch University’s Institute for Science and Technology Policy (ISTP) has demonstrated that public transport is more efficient than cars.
column2: 默多克大学科学技术政策研究所（ISTP）为世界银行开展的一项新研究表明，公共交通比汽车更高效。
column5: Institute for Science and Technology Policy|n. 科学技术政策研究所

column1: The study compared the proportion of wealth poured into transport by thirty-seven cities around the world.
column2: 这项研究比较了世界各地37座城市各自投入交通的资金占其财富的比例。

column1: This included both the public and private costs of building, maintaining and using a transport system.
column2: 计算在内的有建设、维护和使用交通系统的成本，既包括公共支出，也包括私人支出。
column4: both the public and private costs|公共和私人两方面的成本

column1: The study found that the Western Australian city of Perth is a good example of a city with minimal public transport.
column2: 研究发现，西澳大利亚州的珀斯就是公共交通服务十分有限的城市的一个典型例子。
column4: Western Australian|adj. 西澳大利亚州的
column5: a good example of|……的典型例子
column6: minimal|adj. 极少的；十分有限的

column1: As a result, 17% of its wealth went into transport costs.
column2: 因此，珀斯有17%的财富花在了交通上。

column1: Some European and Asian cities, on the other hand, spent as little as 5%.
column2: 相比之下，有些欧洲和亚洲城市花在交通上的比例低至5%。
column5: on the other hand|相比之下

column1: Professor Peter Newman, ISTP Director, pointed out that these more efficient cities were able to put the difference into attracting industry and jobs or creating a better place to live.
column2: 研究所所长彼得·纽曼教授指出，这些交通效率较高的城市可以把省下的钱用于吸引产业和就业机会，或改善居住环境。
column7: the difference|n. 两项交通开支之间的差额
column11: a better place to live|更宜居的地方

column1: According to Professor Newman, the larger Australian city of Melbourne is a rather unusual city in this sort of comparison.
column2: 据纽曼教授说，澳大利亚的墨尔本规模更大，在这类比较中是个颇不寻常的例子。

column1: He describes it as two cities: ‘A European city surrounded by a car-dependent one’.
column2: 他把墨尔本形容为两座城：“一座欧洲式城市，外围又是一座依赖汽车的城市。”

column1: Melbourne’s large tram network has made car use in the inner city much lower, but the outer suburbs have the same car-based structure as most other Australian cities.
column2: 墨尔本庞大的有轨电车网络使内城区的汽车使用率低得多；但外围郊区和澳大利亚大多数其他城市一样，仍以汽车为中心布局。
column3: tram network|n. 有轨电车网络
column4: car use|n. 汽车使用情况

column1: The explosion in demand for accommodation in the inner suburbs of Melbourne suggests a recent change in many people’s preferences as to where they live.
column2: 墨尔本近郊的住房需求激增，表明近来许多人对居住地点的偏好发生了变化。

column1: Newman says this is a new, broader way of considering public transport issues.
column2: 纽曼说，这提供了一个看待公共交通问题的新视角，而且比以往更宽广。
column3: a new, broader way|一种更宽广的新视角

column1: In the past, the case for public transport has been made on the basis of environmental and social justice considerations rather than economics.
column2: 过去，人们为公共交通辩护，依据的是对环境和社会公平的考虑，而非经济因素。
column5: on the basis of|以……为依据

column1: Newman, however, believes the study demonstrates that ‘the auto-dependent city model is inefficient and grossly inadequate in economic as well as environmental terms’.
column2: 纽曼则认为，研究表明，“依赖汽车的城市模式效率低下，而且从经济和环境两方面看都极不理想”。

column1: Bicycle use was not included in the study but Newman noted that the two most ‘bicycle friendly’ cities considered – Amsterdam and Copenhagen – were very efficient, even though their public transport systems were ‘reasonable but not special’.
column2: 该研究没有把自行车出行纳入统计。但纽曼指出，在纳入考察的城市中，对骑自行车最友好的两座——阿姆斯特丹和哥本哈根——交通效率很高，尽管它们的公共交通系统只算“尚可，没什么特别”。
column6: bicycle friendly|adj. 适合骑自行车的
column8: Amsterdam and Copenhagen|n. 阿姆斯特丹和哥本哈根
column11: public transport systems|n. 公共交通系统
column12: reasonable but not special|尚可但并不特别

column1: It is common for supporters of road networks to reject the models of cities with good public transport by arguing that such systems would not work in their particular city.
column2: 支持发展道路网的人常常不接受公共交通发达城市的做法，理由是那样的交通系统在他们自己的城市行不通。
column10: particular city|n. 自己的那座城市

column1: One objection is climate.
column2: 有人以气候为由提出反对。

column1: Some people say their city could not make more use of public transport because it is either too hot or too cold.
column2: 有人说，自己的城市不是太热就是太冷，所以无法更多地利用公共交通。
column3: make more use of|更多地利用
column5: either too hot or too cold|要么太热，要么太冷

column1: Newman rejects this, pointing out that public transport has been successful in both Toronto and Singapore and, in fact, he has checked the use of cars against climate and found ‘zero correlation’.
column2: 纽曼不同意这种说法。他指出，公共交通在多伦多和新加坡都很成功；事实上，他比较过汽车使用情况和气候，发现两者的“相关性为零”。

column1: When it comes to other physical features, road lobbies are on stronger ground.
column2: 说到其他地理条件，主张发展公路的游说团体就更有理由了。
column3: When it comes to|说到；谈及
column4: physical features|n. 地形等自然条件
column5: road lobbies|n. 主张发展公路的游说团体
column6: on stronger ground|论据更充分；更站得住脚

column1: For example, Newman accepts it would be hard for a city as hilly as Auckland to develop a really good rail network.
column2: 比如，纽曼承认，像奥克兰这样丘陵密布的城市，要建成一个真正出色的铁路网确实很难。
column5: as hilly as|和……一样多丘陵

column1: However, he points out that both Hong Kong and Zurich have managed to make a success of their rail systems, heavy and light respectively, though there are few cities in the world as hilly.
column2: 不过，他指出，香港的重轨和苏黎世的轻轨都办得很成功，尽管世界上很少有城市像它们这样多丘陵。
column5: make a success of|把……办成功
column6: rail systems|n. 轨道交通系统

column1: In fact, Newman believes the main reason for adopting one sort of transport over another is politics: ‘The more democratic the process, the more public transport is favored.’
column2: 实际上，纽曼认为，城市选择某种交通方式而舍弃另一种，主要出于政治原因：“决策过程越民主，公共交通就越受支持。”

column1: He considers Portland, Oregon, a perfect example of this.
column2: 他认为，俄勒冈州的波特兰市就是一个绝佳的例子。
column6: a perfect example of|……的绝佳例子

column1: Some years ago, federal money was granted to build a new road.
column2: 多年前，联邦政府曾拨款修建一条新路。

column1: However, local pressure groups forced a referendum over whether to spend the money on light rail instead.
column2: 但在当地倡议团体的推动下，是否改用这笔钱修轻轨，必须交由公民投票决定。
column4: pressure groups|n. 倡议团体；施压团体
column8: spend the money on|把这笔钱用于

column1: The rail proposal won and the railway worked spectacularly well.
column2: 轻轨方案赢得了公投，建成后运营得非常成功。

column1: In the years that have followed, more and more rail systems have been put in, dramatically changing the nature of the city.
column2: 此后几年，越来越多的轨道交通系统建了起来，城市的面貌也随之大为改观。
column3: In the years that have followed|在此后的几年里
column5: rail systems|n. 轨道交通系统
column8: nature of the city|城市的面貌与特点

column1: Newman notes that Portland has about the same population as Perth and had a similar population density at the time.
column2: 纽曼指出，波特兰目前的人口与珀斯大致相当，当时两市的人口密度也相近。
column4: about the same population as|人口与……大致相同

column1: In the UK, travel times to work had been stable for at least six centuries, with people avoiding situations that required them to spend more than half an hour travelling to work.
column2: 在英国，通勤时间曾至少六个世纪保持稳定，人们会避免需要花半个多小时去上班的情形。
column3: travel times to work|n. 通勤时间
column9: more than half an hour|超过半小时

column1: Trains and cars initially allowed people to live at greater distances without taking longer to reach their destination.
column2: 起初，火车和汽车让人们可以住得更远，而到达目的地所用的时间并没有变长。
column5: live at greater distances|住得更远
column6: without taking longer|用时并未增加

column1: However, public infrastructure did not keep pace with urban sprawl, causing massive congestion problems which now make commuting times far higher.
column2: 然而，公共基础设施没有跟上城市向外扩张的速度，造成了严重的交通拥堵，如今人们的通勤时间因此长了许多。
column3: public infrastructure|n. 公共基础设施
column5: urban sprawl|n. 城市向外蔓延
column10: far higher|高得多（指通勤时间更长）

column1: There is a widespread belief that increasing wealth encourages people to live farther out where cars are the only viable transport.
column2: 人们普遍认为，财富增加会促使人们搬到离市中心更远的地方，而在那里，汽车是唯一可行的交通工具。

column1: The example of European cities refutes that.
column2: 欧洲城市的例子驳斥了这种看法。

column1: They are often wealthier than their American counterparts but have not generated the same level of car use.
column2: 这些欧洲城市往往比美国的同类城市更富裕，但其汽车使用量并没有美国城市那么高。
column4: American counterparts|n. 美国的同类城市
column6: the same level of|同等程度的

column1: In Stockholm, car use has actually fallen in recent years as the city has become larger and wealthier.
column2: 近年来，斯德哥尔摩规模扩大、财富增加，汽车使用量却实际下降了。

column1: A new study makes this point even more starkly.
column2: 一项新研究更鲜明地说明了这一点。

column1: Developing cities in Asia, such as Jakarta and Bangkok, make more use of the car than wealthy Asian cities such as Tokyo and Singapore.
column2: 雅加达和曼谷等发展中的亚洲城市，比东京和新加坡等富裕的亚洲城市更常使用汽车。
column3: Developing cities|n. 发展中的城市
column5: make more use of|更多地使用

column1: In cities that developed later, the World Bank and Asian Development Bank discouraged the building of public transport and people have been forced to rely on cars – creating the massive traffic jams that characterize those cities.
column2: 在发展较晚的城市，世界银行和亚洲开发银行不鼓励建设公共交通。人们被迫依赖汽车，造成了这些城市典型的严重交通拥堵。
column5: Asian Development Bank|n. 亚洲开发银行
column10: massive traffic jams|n. 严重交通拥堵

column1: Newman believes one of the best studies on how cities built for cars might be converted to rail use is The Urban Village report, which used Melbourne as an example.
column2: 纽曼认为，《城市村落》报告是探讨如何让原本围绕汽车建设的城市转向轨道交通的最佳研究之一。这份报告以墨尔本为例。
column3: one of the best studies|最佳研究之一
column4: built for cars|围绕汽车而建设的
column7: rail use|n. 轨道交通的使用

column1: It found that pushing everyone into the city centre was not the best approach.
column2: 报告发现，让所有人都集中到市中心并非最佳办法。
column4: pushing everyone into|促使所有人集中到

column1: Instead, the proposal advocated the creation of urban villages at hundreds of sites, mostly around railway stations.
column2: 报告主张在数百处地点建设城市村落，选址大多在火车站周边。

column1: It was once assumed that improvements in telecommunications would lead to more dispersal in the population as people were no longer forced into cities.
column2: 人们一度以为，通信技术的进步会让人口分布更分散，因为人们再也不必聚居在城市里。
column10: forced into cities|不得不聚居到城市中

column1: However, the ISTP team’s research demonstrates that the population and job density of cities rose or remained constant in the 1980s after decades of decline.
column2: 然而，该研究所的研究表明，经过数十年的下降后，城市的人口密度和就业岗位密度在20世纪80年代有所回升，或维持不变。
column5: population and job density|n. 人口密度和就业岗位密度
column9: decades of decline|数十年的下降

column1: The explanation for this seems to be that it is valuable to place people working in related fields together.
column2: 原因似乎在于，让从事相关领域工作的人聚集在一起很有价值。

column1: ‘The new world will largely depend on human creativity, and creativity flourishes where people come together face-to-face.’
column2: “新世界将在很大程度上依赖人类的创造力，而创造力在人们面对面相聚时最为蓬勃。”
column6: human creativity|n. 人类的创造力
